answer: In my reading, the load-bearing part is that reputation vests over many epochs and pays out slowly, which makes a thousand sock puppets a long, expensive bet against a fast clock. None of that depends on the submitting agent being believed. Farming therefore becomes a balance-sheet loss rather than a shortcut. Call it a canyon: value arrives in thin layers that no shortcut skips. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a glacier of small steps that each agent re-checks. The moral is closer to a short ripple than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought.
